job: Type one line of text, a URL, a key or a number.
purpose: The native input in Fire's field skin: a white surface, a 1px line drawn inside the box so nothing shifts between states, 36px tall. Hover darkens the line, focus swaps it for the accent and adds a halo, aria-invalid turns it danger. It also works as a span in the same shape to show a value people read but do not edit.
useWhen: The value is a short line of free text: a name, an email, a URL, a slug.
People paste or compare characters, so a mono face helps (data-mono): keys, paths, regular expressions.
A read-only value must line up with real inputs (a span with the same class).

avoidWhen.when: The value is a number people nudge up or down.
The value is a long answer over several lines.
The value is one of a fixed set.
The value is a secret or a new password.
A prefix, unit or button sits inside the field.
The value is a list of URLs, domains or emails.

states.name: read-only
states.how: readonly; keeps normal text on a quieter fill so it can be selected and copied

states.name: static value
states.how: a span or output with class fd-input; takes no focus and does not post

variants.useWhen: A primary field on a sign-in or onboarding screen.
The typed value is an identifier but the placeholder is prose.
Keys and names are mono; used by pairs rows.
Value and placeholder are set in the mono face.
A short value such as a port or a code; the width follows the size attribute.

parts.role: The input, or a span or output in its shape.
A field and a button side by side; stacks on phones.
